summary: CCC-built 1934 three-story NPS Rustic lookout in Yosemite National Park, used for fire detection into the 1960s-70s, NRHP-eligible, cab now reserved for emergency use.

facts.design: Three-story NPS Rustic-style lookout: garage on the first floor, living quarters on the second, and a 13 x 13 ft cab with a catwalk on top

access.note: Register says the cab is now reserved for emergency use; a hiking route of about 0.7 miles from Yosemite West reaches the tower.

visit.trail_note: Unmarked trailhead at the end of Azalea Lane in Yosemite West; asphalt access road past water towers, then about 0.7 miles on foot to the lookout.

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps as a three-story NPS Rustic lookout.
Used by the National Park Service for fire detection in the 1960s and 1970s; sources differ on when the watch ended.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on June 4, 1998.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia says the lookout was used for fire detection in the 1960s and 1970s and was still in use in the 1980s. Qualla places its fire-watch role in the 1960s and 1970s. The register says the cab is now reserved for emergency use. The story reports the span as stated and flags the 1980s claim as disputed.

notes_for_editor: Build year 1934 and the June 4, 1998 registration are confirmed by NHLR. A Living New Deal page (livingnewdeal.org) reportedly says the tower was used until 1966 and is now empty; the fetch returned HTTP 403 and the search snippet was not quoted, so it is not used. Last-use dates conflict across sources (1966, 1970s, 1980s) and the story says so. No current NPS status page or recent access notice was read, so the access level rests on the register text and the Wikipedia trail description. The restoration year is not given in any source read, so no restored event was added. Qualla is a secondary travel page; its quotes are used only for the 1960s-70s fire-watch role.
